doc.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Sneaking off to the Howard Theatre to hear Nancy Wilson, Miles and others
summary: As a teenager he told his parents he was going to the theater and instead heard Nancy Wilson, Quincy Jones and Miles.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well I guess it is at that. But I used to, when I was in high school, I was right outside Washington where the Howard Theatre is. And I used to tell my mother and father, “I’m going to the theater tonight.” They thought I was going to go see a Roy Rogers thing. I’d © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

probably go to hear Shorty Rogers or somebody. I heard Nancy Wilson when she was maybe 21, right after she had done the two Capitol albums. And she was eight feet tall and weighed a hundred and fifteen pounds and pure dynamite in a floor length blue dress. And the curtain opened and the audience went [gasp], and she slayed them. And I heard Redd Foxx, I heard Moms Mabley, I heard Quincy Jones’ big band, I heard Miles with, I think, Cannonball and Coltrane and I’m pretty sure Bill Evans but my memory of the sidemen back then — this was at a time when I was still trying to figure out where Trane stopped and Cannonball came in. I was still trying to sort out the difference between the sound of a tenor and an alto because I was just, you know. But I would show up two hours early to go hear — and even later on when I was legal to get into bars I’d go to hear Miles. I’d show up at eight o’clock. I’d be at the table at eight for a nine o’clock set. I was so infected by the whole thing.
[I’m sorry, we just lost your mic, Monk]
